LESSON: IMITATIVE SPEAKING: PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.2: Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 7 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: where do your parents work?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify family members by their names and professions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply appropriate intonation and stress in pronouncing words for fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the role of immediate family members for social co- existence.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

A. identify family members by their names and professions,

B. apply appropriate intonation and stress in pronouncing words for fluency,

   Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the role of immediate family members for social co- existence.
